fragments.text: ㊩ There's some error in the behaviour of starting and stopping codex autorunner in the codex-19 REPL .
I stopped it and it didn't stop, first of all, and the 象 didn't turn gray second of all.

reply_text:
Stopping the autorunner only works in the buffer where you run the command: the "on" flag and the pending timer belong to that buffer. Next I'll look at codex-19's live state in your Emacs.Every codex buffer now shows the autorunner off, and your stop commands did run in codex-19. Next I'll check codex-19's own trace for what happened after you stopped it.A turn is still running in codex-19 right now (last trace entry 05:10). Next I'll check whether that turn was sent by the autorunner after you stopped it, or was already in flight.The current turn was sent with the autorunner's prompt ("OK please continue"). Next I'll check whether anything besides the Emacs timer sends that prompt.The "Last: analysed" line in codex-19's indicator was about a claude-4 turn: that status is shared across buffers. Next I'll read codex-19's own turn records.The autorunner sent the 05:06 "OK please continue" turn: its record is marked not-requested. That turn is still running. Next I'll check whether anything new gets sent once it finishes.㊥ The autorunner in codex-19 is off and won't send again, but I can't yet tell whether it ever sent after you stopped it. Did a new "OK please continue" appear *after* one of your stops, or did the turn that was already running just keep going? Stopping only cancels the next send; a running turn carries on until it finishes or you press C-c C-c. On the colour: grey means the autorunner is *on*, so after a stop it should go back to red, not grey.

㊩: (it didn't stop) Here's what I can see:
- Your stop ran in codex-19: *Messages* has "stopped in codex-19" four times.
- The autorunner is now fully off there: the flag is nil, no timer is pending, and its hook is gone. The same holds in every other codex buffer.
- The last autorunner turn was sent at 05:06 and was still running at 05:12.
- What I can't recover is when you pressed stop. The buffer's trace keeps only 20 entries, and the stop lines have already scrolled out.
- I read the stop code: it cancels the pending timer and the hook, and the send path checks the flag again before sending. I found no way for a send to get past a stop.

So my best guess is that the 05:06 turn was still running when you stopped, and stopping gave no sign that it would let that turn finish.

㊩: (the 象 didn't turn gray) The 象 indicator itself works. I evaluated it in codex-19 with the autorunner on and got gray50; with it off it's red, which is what it showed.
- Grey means "autorunner on, its repeated prompt isn't read" (or 象 is switched off).
- Red is normal reading, so red is the right colour after a stop.

If what you saw was red while it was still running, the likely cause is that the indicator only redrew on the next output.

㊢ (fix) The fix is futon3c `40f8a2e1`, and both functions are already loaded into your Emacs.
- Start and stop now redraw the 象 indicator immediately.
- If a turn is still running when you stop, the message says "the current turn will finish (C-c C-c interrupts it)".

I haven't changed stop to interrupt the running turn. That would cut off work in progress, and it's your call whether stop should do that.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the report changes in the strategy) Three findings matter for the proposal model.
- **The example is a recording failure.** Turn 391 is an instance of a fourth outcome: accepted but not recorded. The parser of the time didn't accept the answer, and `turn-ports` ran without links. If we count outcomes before fixing that, accepted proposals will be counted as unanswered.
- **The record can't settle decline versus neglect.** Q7 says that if you skip proposals *because* you'd decline them, the record can never separate the two (Mohan–Pearl, self-masking). The only remedy is an ask that fires independently of the expected answer. So the ask arm in M-zaif-harness has a second job: making the response model learnable at all.
- **"Did you see it" needs its own node.** "Unseen" and "seen, no response" need separate mechanisms. The voxterm observable I mentioned (a proposal outside the first paragraph may never be spoken) is a direct stand-in for whether you saw it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(order of work)
1. Make 大象 and the kernel record colon-form answers and links on every turn. That prevents the turn-391 mistake.
2. Count last week's agent ㊭ paragraphs into: accepted, declined, no response with the proposal in the gist, no response with it out of the gist.
3. Build the model with a seen node, which the report says fits the Markov setting directly.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (Answer to §1) The report's headline answer is that no single category holds a War Machine click, a 象 standing, a pattern cascade and the operator's response as the same kind of thing. They share one floor of probabilistic channels, and three pieces attach outside it: the War Machine's choice between policies, the 象 standing, and the operator as an agent. Nothing on the site claims one unified model, so the copy doesn't need changing.
